docs.title: Abstract
docs.text: This document specifies the core structures and processing rules for transaction authentication using [OID4VP] and [OID4VCI]. It defines the roles involved, the governance framework for credentials and transaction data types, the holder binding proof structure, and the transaction data processing pipeline. While designed with payments and Strong Customer Authentication in mind, PaSO is applicable to any domain requiring verifiable, user-consented transactions.

docs.title: 1.1 Overview
docs.text:
PaSO (Payments and SCA for OpenID) extends [OID4VP] and [OID4VCI] for verifiable, user-consented transactions. More specifically, it defines a framework to allow using wallets as Strong Customer Authentication and payment means in the context of [PSD2]. [OID4VP] defines the transaction_data parameter but leaves its processing, display, and proof semantics open. PaSO fills these gaps with a minimum viable set of structures and rules.

This document, PaSO Core, defines:

  • the roles participating in a PaSO transaction,
  • what Credential Rulebooks and Transaction Data Type Rulebooks are,
  • the holder binding proof structure produced by the Wallet,
  • the transaction data processing pipeline.

docs.title: 1.2 Scope
docs.text:
PaSO Core does not define metadata infrastructure (serving, signing, or discovery of credential metadata), rendering implementations, transaction logging, or trust establishment. These are addressed by other PaSO specifications.

The Wallet and the Attestation Provider are expected to agree on a mechanism to ensure the integrity of the Wallet environment. A common approach is a long-lived wallet unit attestation that is revoked if integrity can no longer be guaranteed.

docs.title: 1.3 Requirements Notation
docs.text: The key words "MUST", "MUST NOT", "REQUIRED", "SHALL", "SHALL NOT", "SHOULD", "SHOULD NOT", "RECOMMENDED", "MAY", and "OPTIONAL" in this document are to be interpreted as described in [RFC2119] and [RFC8174] when, and only when, they are written in all capital letters.

docs.title: 1.4 Terminology
docs.text: Term Definition PaSO Credential A credential used with PaSO. Issued by an Attestation Provider into a Wallet and presented to a Relying Party with transaction data and a holder binding proof. Dynamic Linking The cryptographic binding of transaction-specific data to the presentation proof, ensuring that the data the user consented to is tamper-evident and verifiable. In the context of [PSD2] Article 97(2), this specifically requires linking to a specific amount and a specific payee. Strong Customer Authentication (SCA) Authentication using at least two elements from different categories (knowledge, possession, inherence) that are independent of each other, per [PSD2] Article 97. Credential Rulebook A governance document that defines the rules for issuing, displaying, and verifying a credential type. See Section 4. Transaction Data Type Rulebook A governance document that defines the semantic meaning and structure of a specific transaction data type. See Section 5. Risk Signal Profile A published governance document that bundles risk signal types — defined in [PaSO Risk Signal Registry] — with a per-signal requirement flag and an optional freshness bound. Referenced by signed credential metadata or a Transaction Data Type Rulebook. See [PaSO Risk Signals] Section 3. Authorizing Party The party that receives the proof package from the Relying Party, verifies the transaction, and authorizes the action. See Section 2.

docs.title: 2 Roles
docs.text:
The following roles participate in PaSO transactions:

  • Attestation Provider: Defined as the Credential Issuer in [OID4VCI]. Issues PaSO Credentials into the Wallet.
  • Wallet: Defined as the Wallet in [OID4VP]. Stores PaSO Credentials, processes transaction data, and produces the holder binding proof.
  • Relying Party: Defined as the Verifier in [OID4VP]. Sends presentation requests containing transaction data and receives the verifiable presentation.
  • Authorizing Party: The party that ultimately authorizes the transaction. It receives the proof package from the Relying Party and verifies it in conjunction with the original presentation request. The Authorizing Party has a trust relationship with the Attestation Provider and the Relying Party.

docs.title: 3 Flows
docs.text:
Two common flow types are expected in the PaSO ecosystem:

  • First-party flow: A single party fulfils the roles of Attestation Provider, Relying Party, and Authorizing Party. The Wallet presents the PaSO Credential back to the party that issued it.

  • Third-party flow: The Relying Party is distinct from the Attestation Provider and Authorizing Party. The Wallet presents the PaSO Credential to the Relying Party, which forwards the proof package to the Authorizing Party.

The Relying Party SHALL send a signed [OID4VP] Authorization Request (Request Object per [JAR]). The Wallet SHALL reject unsigned PaSO presentation requests.

docs.title: 4.1 Purpose
docs.text: A Credential Rulebook is a governance document that defines the rules for a specific PaSO Credential type. Every PaSO Credential type SHOULD have a Credential Rulebook.

docs.title: 4.2 Contents
docs.text:
A Credential Rulebook MAY specify:

  • The nature of a PaSO Credential and its applicable contexts,
  • attribute structures for the PaSO Credential,
  • display rules for the credential in the Wallet,
  • references to one or more Transaction Data Type Rulebooks,
  • policies for Attestation Providers and Relying Parties,
  • issuance requirements (e.g., validity period, binding to wallet attestations),
  • holder binding and user authentication requirements: how the credential key is protected and which user authentication releases it,
  • verification requirements for the Relying Party and Authorizing Party,
  • the embedded disclosure policy, if applicable.

Strong Customer Authentication is established by holder binding: the credential key is held in the Wallet's secure cryptographic environment (possession) and released only after user authentication (knowledge or inherence). The Credential Rulebook of a PaSO Credential used for Strong Customer Authentication SHALL specify the holder binding and user authentication requirements by which its presentations meet [PSD2] Article 97.

Attestation Providers and Relying Parties SHALL follow the applicable Credential Rulebook.

docs.title: 5.1 Purpose
docs.text:
A Transaction Data Type Rulebook is a governance document that defines a specific transaction data type. It specifies the semantic meaning of all claims and all UI display requirements.

Every transaction data type identifier used with PaSO SHALL have a Transaction Data Type Rulebook published by the organisation that owns the identifier, except a type used only with ad-hoc metadata per [PaSO Proof Metadata] Section 5. For such a type, the ad-hoc metadata supplied by the Relying Party is the complete definition of the type for the transaction it accompanies, and the immutability requirement of Section 5.3 does not apply.

docs.title: 5.2 Type Identifiers
docs.text:
Each PaSO transaction data type is identified by a URN following this structure:

urn:paso:sca:<domain>:<suffix>:<version>

Where:

  • <domain> is an organisation identifier in reverse domain notation (e.g., com.example), or global for transaction data types defined by PaSO itself,
  • <suffix> is one or more colon-separated segments identifying the type (e.g., payment),
  • <version> is a version number (e.g., 1). It SHALL be a positive integer without leading zeros and SHALL be the final segment of the identifier. New versions of a transaction data type SHALL use monotonically increasing integers.

The Wallet identifies PaSO transaction data entries by checking whether the type field starts with the prefix urn:paso:sca:.

docs.title: 5.3 Rulebook Requirements
docs.text:
A Transaction Data Type Rulebook SHALL define, for each claim in the transaction data type:

  • the semantic meaning of the claim,
  • whether the claim is required or optional in the transaction payload,
  • whether the claim must be displayed to the user,
  • how the claim value is to be rendered when displayed.

A Transaction Data Type Rulebook MAY also define the localised UI labels for the consent screen, including at minimum a label for the confirmation action.

A Transaction Data Type Rulebook MAY include a Static Presentation section, which enables static rendering of the transaction data type per [PaSO View] Section 5. A Static Presentation section SHALL define:

  • which claims SHALL be displayed in static rendering, and which claims MAY be omitted,
  • the display obligations for each displayed claim, such as prominence and completeness,
  • the meaning of the affirmative action and of the denial action.

These definitions, including any Static Presentation section, constitute the semantic structure of the transaction data type. For any given type identifier, the semantic structure SHALL be immutable once published. Changes to the semantic structure SHALL require a new version of the type identifier.

The Wallet SHALL ensure that all claims designated for display — in static rendering, those that the Static Presentation section requires — have been shown to the user before enabling the confirmation action.

docs.title: 5.4 Content Quality
docs.text: All text displayed to the user SHALL be short and easily understandable.

docs.title: 5.5 Rulebook Obligations
docs.text:
Conformance to a Transaction Data Type Rulebook is ensured by the parties that construct and verify transaction data:

  • The Attestation Provider SHALL ensure that the transaction_data_types entry it publishes for a transaction data type in the signed credential metadata ([PaSO Proof Metadata] Section 3) is consistent with the rulebook. This includes the claims and which of them are required, and any risk signal profiles, risk signals and encryption that the rulebook requires ([PaSO Risk Signals]).
  • The Relying Party SHALL construct the payload of a transaction_data entry per the rulebook of its type. For a type used only with ad-hoc metadata (Section 5.1), it SHALL construct the payload per that metadata. Where it supplies ad-hoc metadata ([PaSO Proof Metadata] Section 5) for a type that has a rulebook, it SHALL ensure that the metadata is consistent with the rulebook, as the Attestation Provider must for the metadata it publishes.
  • The Authorizing Party SHALL verify that the payload conforms to the rulebook, per [PaSO Proof Verify] Section 3.

A Wallet implements a rulebook by building it in; it does not obtain rulebooks at runtime. The Wallet SHALL apply the requirements of every rulebook it implements. For a rulebook it does not implement, the Wallet relies on the credential metadata, which reflects the rulebook by the Attestation Provider's obligation above.

docs.title: 6.1 SCA Response Claims
docs.text:
The Wallet SHALL include the following claims in every PaSO Credential presentation that involves transaction data, embedded in the format-specific proof structure that cryptographically binds the user's consent to the presentation.

Claim Required Description jti yes A fresh, cryptographically random value with sufficient entropy per [RFC7519] Section 4.1.7. Unique per presentation. When used for SCA, serves as the Authentication Code per [PSD2]. display_locale yes The locale of the consent screen shown to the user. For dynamic rendering, per [PaSO View] Section 4: the [RFC5646] language tag of the selected display and ui_labels entries as it appears in the metadata, or the string default if the default entries (entries without a locale) were shown. For static rendering, per [PaSO View] Section 5.4: an [RFC5646] language tag, never default. Enables deterministic reconstruction of which text was shown. render_mode yes The rendering mode used for the transaction data shown during consent: dynamic or static, per [PaSO View] Section 5.2. transaction_data_hash yes Hash, computed with transaction_data_hash_alg, of the transaction_data entry selected for the PaSO Credential, taken over its base64url-encoded string exactly as it appears in the transaction_data request parameter. No base64url decoding is performed before hashing. transaction_data_hash_alg yes Hash algorithm identifier, a "Hash Name String" from the IANA "Named Information Hash Algorithm" registry. SHALL be sha-256, unless the applicable Transaction Data Type Rulebook names another algorithm. metadata_integrity yes The [W3C.SRI] integrity value of the signed credential metadata JWT (per [PaSO Proof Metadata]) relied on during this presentation: the JWT used to display the transaction data or, where ad-hoc metadata was used, the JWT that authorised the Relying Party to supply it per [PaSO Proof Metadata] Section 5.4. request_integrity yes The [W3C.SRI] integrity value of the signed [OID4VP] Authorization Request ([JAR] Request Object) as received by the Wallet, computed over the compact-serialised JWT string. wallet_instance_version yes Version identifier of the Wallet application that authorized the transaction. risk_signals conditional An array of risk-signal envelopes per [PaSO Risk Signals]. REQUIRED when the signal set resolved for the matched transaction data type contains one or more required signals, per [PaSO Risk Signals] Section 4.1; absent otherwise. Signal types are defined by [PaSO Risk Signal Registry]. When encryption is required for the transaction data type, this value is an encrypted structure per [PaSO Risk Signals] instead of a plaintext array.

The authentication methods used to release the transaction, and the response_mode of the Authorization Request, are not claims of this section. They are risk signal types defined by [PaSO Risk Signal Registry] and are carried inside risk_signals when the risk signal set in force requires them. Strong Customer Authentication is established by holder binding per Section 4.2. The authentication-methods signal is a Wallet observation like any other risk signal: its presence does not establish Strong Customer Authentication, and its absence does not negate it.

These claims are PaSO's representation of the transaction data in the presentation, which [OID4VP] Section 8.4 leaves to the transaction data type. PaSO does not use the transaction_data_hashes and transaction_data_hashes_alg parameters of [OID4VP] Appendix B.3.3.1.

docs.title: 6.2 SD-JWT-VC Profile
docs.text: For PaSO Credentials in [SD-JWT-VC] format, the Wallet SHALL include a Key Binding JWT (KB-JWT). The SCA response claims from Section 6.1 SHALL be included as top-level claims in the KB-JWT payload, in addition to the standard KB-JWT claims defined by [OID4VP].

docs.title: 6.3 mdoc Profile
docs.text:
For PaSO Credentials in [mdoc] format, the Wallet SHALL include device authentication. The SCA response claims SHALL be included as device-signed data elements in the DeviceNameSpaces structure under the namespace urn:paso:sca:1.

Data element CBOR type jti tstr display_locale tstr render_mode tstr transaction_data_hash bstr transaction_data_hash_alg tstr metadata_integrity tstr request_integrity tstr wallet_instance_version tstr risk_signals array of maps

docs.title: 7.1 Transaction Data Object
docs.text:
PaSO extends the [OID4VP] transaction_data entry with the following parameter:

  • payload: REQUIRED. A JSON object containing the transaction details. The structure is defined by the applicable Transaction Data Type Rulebook for the matching type.

docs.title: 7.2 Locale Selection
docs.text: For dynamic rendering, locale selection SHALL follow [PaSO View] Section 4. The Wallet renders all display and ui_labels entries from a single locale, selected with the Lookup matching scheme defined in [RFC4647] Section 3.4. If no locale in its priority list matches, it renders all of them from the default entries (entries without a locale); if not every array has a default entry, the entry is not compatible with the credential ([PaSO View] Section 4). The selection SHALL be reported in the display_locale claim (Section 6.1): the selected metadata locale tag, or the string default. It reflects the entries actually rendered, not the priority-list locale that led to the selection. For static rendering, display_locale is determined per [PaSO View] Section 5.4.

docs.title: 7.3 Simple Profile
docs.text:
The simple profile is the minimum PaSO transaction data processing mode and a minimal subset of the advanced profile. All Wallets supporting PaSO SHALL implement the simple profile. A Wallet implementing the advanced profile is fully compatible with requests made in the simple profile.

In the simple profile, the presentation request contains exactly one PaSO-targeted transaction_data entry, identified by a type starting with urn:paso:sca:, whose credential_ids SHALL contain exactly one credential query identifier; that credential query SHALL NOT set multiple to true ([OID4VP] Section 6.1). When credential_sets are used, that credential query identifier SHALL appear in every option of every credential set that references it, and at least one such credential set SHALL be required; the options SHALL be transposable as defined in Section 7.4.1. A request that does not meet these conditions is not in the simple profile (Section 7.4).

The Wallet SHALL:

  1. Identify the credentials in the Wallet that match the credential query.
  2. Retain those credentials with which the entry is compatible per Section 7.5. If none remain, the Wallet SHALL cease processing and inform the user.
  3. If more than one credential remains, let the user select one. The Wallet SHALL display the transaction data as rendered with the selected credential's metadata and SHALL update the display when the selection changes.
  4. Display the transaction data to the user for consent.
  5. If the user consents, proceed with the presentation.

docs.title: 7.4 Advanced Profile
docs.text:
The advanced profile applies when a presentation request contains a PaSO-targeted transaction_data entry and does not meet the conditions of the simple profile (Section 7.3). Wallets MAY implement the advanced profile. Credential Rulebooks and Transaction Data Type Rulebooks MAY require that the Wallet supports the advanced profile.

A Wallet that does not support the advanced profile SHALL reject such a presentation request and SHALL inform the user.

docs.title: 7.4.1 Transaction Data and DCQL Credential Sets
docs.text:
The presentation request MAY contain multiple PaSO-targeted transaction_data entries.

When credential_sets are used in the DCQL query ([OID4VP] Section 6.2), all credential query identifiers referenced by PaSO-targeted transaction_data entries' credential_ids SHALL appear within options of the same credential set.

Each inner array within the options of the credential set (hereafter called an alternative) lists credential query identifiers that MUST all be presented together. An alternative resolves to a PaSO-targeted transaction_data entry if it contains a credential query identifier listed in that entry's credential_ids. When an alternative resolves to multiple PaSO-targeted transaction_data entries for the same credential, the Wallet SHALL apply the first-match selection rule from Section 7.4.2 step 2.

All alternatives that involve a PaSO-targeted transaction_data entry SHALL be transposable. Transposability means that the user's credential choices must be fully independent of each other. Selecting one credential should never constrain which credentials are available in another slot.

Concretely: it must be possible to decompose the alternatives into a set of independent credential slots S₁, S₂, …, Sₖ, where each slot represents one independent choice the user makes. Each slot contains the credentials the user can pick for that choice, and may also allow the user to pick nothing (making that slot optional). A slot contains ∅ when some alternatives contain none of its credential query identifiers. The full list of PaSO-targeted alternatives must be exactly the result of combining every possible selection across all slots.

A Relying Party SHALL construct its alternatives so that this holds. If a Wallet detects that the alternatives cannot be decomposed this way, meaning some credential choices are artificially coupled, it SHALL stop processing and inform the user.

Alternatives that do not involve any PaSO-targeted transaction_data entry are not subject to this requirement.

A presentation request SHALL allow exactly one PaSO Credential to be presented:

  • When credential_sets are used, every alternative of the credential set that contains the credential query identifiers referenced by PaSO-targeted transaction_data entries SHALL contain exactly one of those identifiers, and that credential set SHALL NOT have required set to false ([OID4VP] Section 6.2).
  • When credential_sets are not used, the PaSO-targeted transaction_data entries SHALL together reference exactly one credential query identifier.
  • A credential query referenced by a PaSO-targeted transaction_data entry SHALL NOT set multiple to true ([OID4VP] Section 6.1).

The credential query identifiers referenced by PaSO-targeted transaction_data entries therefore form a single slot without ∅: the PaSO slot. If a Wallet detects that a presentation request does not meet these conditions, it SHALL stop processing and inform the user.

The Wallet SHALL present the PaSO-targeted alternatives to the user as independent choices, one per credential slot. For each slot the user selects one of the available credentials, or none if ∅ is present in that slot. When alternatives resolve to different transaction_data entries, the Wallet SHALL display the transaction data corresponding to the user's current credential selection. When the user changes a selection that causes a different transaction_data entry to apply, the Wallet SHALL update the displayed transaction data accordingly.

The ordering of alternatives expresses the Relying Party's preference: the Wallet SHOULD derive the display order for each slot from the order in which credential query identifiers first appear across the alternatives. The Wallet SHOULD default to the first alternative's selection for each slot, but MAY override the default with a credential the user has previously selected in the same context, provided the slot's display order remains as defined by the request.

A presentation request MAY combine PaSO Credentials with non-PaSO credentials.

docs.title: 7.4.2 Discovery and Validation
docs.text:
The user selects exactly one PaSO Credential, from the PaSO slot (Section 7.4.1). After resolution, exactly one transaction_data entry SHALL apply to that credential. The presentation request MAY contain multiple PaSO-targeted transaction_data entries provided they conform to the rules in Section 7.4.1.

For the PaSO-targeted entries, the Wallet SHALL perform the following steps:

  1. The Wallet SHALL identify all credentials matching the presentation request that are PaSO Credentials. A credential is a candidate for a PaSO-targeted transaction_data entry if the credential matches a credential query whose identifier is listed in that entry's credential_ids.
  2. For each candidate credential, the Wallet SHALL select the first PaSO-targeted transaction_data entry (in array order) that targets that credential via credential_ids and is compatible with it per Section 7.5, evaluating the conditions of Section 7.5 in order. If no entry is compatible, the credential SHALL be excluded.
  3. For each candidate credential, where resolution or verification of an external resource (Section 7.5, condition 4) fails for the selected entry, the entry is incompatible and the Wallet SHALL resume the selection in step 2 for the affected credential, continuing with the next transaction_data entry in array order that targets that credential. If no compatible entry remains for the credential, the credential SHALL be excluded.
  4. If at any point during the processing of this section no compatible credentials remain, the Wallet SHALL cease processing and inform the user.
  5. The Wallet SHALL present the remaining compatible credentials as alternatives to the user. For the initially selected credential, the Wallet SHALL display the transaction_data entry matched in step 2.
  6. If the user selects a different credential, the Wallet SHALL display the transaction_data entry matched for that credential in step 2. When the matched transaction_data entry differs between credentials, the displayed content SHALL update accordingly.
  7. If the user consents, the Wallet MAY proceed with the presentation.

The first-match rule of step 2 allows a Relying Party to provide versioned transaction data: a newer type can be listed first in the transaction_data array, with an older type as a fallback for credentials that do not yet support it (Annex A.7).

docs.title: 7.5 Entry Compatibility
docs.text:
This section applies to both the simple and the advanced profile. A PaSO-targeted transaction_data entry is compatible with a credential when all of the following hold:

  1. The credential matches a credential query whose identifier is listed in the entry's credential_ids.
  2. The entry's type is among the transaction data types supported by the credential.
  3. The payload conforms to the definition of that type. A payload conforms if it does not contain fields not covered by a claim path in the applicable claims metadata (companion #integrity fields are covered by the path of the claim they accompany), all fields declared as required are present, all display formatting directives are supported by the Wallet, and all values conform to their declared formatting. Where the Wallet implements the rulebook of the type (Section 5.5), the payload conforms only if, in addition, every field it contains is declared or permitted by the rulebook.
  4. Every claim of the payload that requires resolution of an external resource with integrity verification has been resolved, and its content verified.

A Wallet SHALL reject a request whose transaction_data entry contains an object with duplicate member names (compared after unescaping).

Other PaSO specifications define further conditions under which an entry is not compatible with a credential.

Failures during transaction data processing have one of three consequences:

  • Request. Where the presentation request itself is malformed or untrusted, whatever the credential, the Wallet rejects it: an unsigned request (Section 3), a request in a profile the Wallet does not support (Section 7.4), alternatives that are not transposable or do not form a single PaSO slot (Section 7.4.1), and duplicate member names (above).
  • Credential. Where the credential itself cannot be used, the Wallet excludes it from further processing: its signed credential metadata JWT is invalid ([PaSO Proof Metadata] Section 7).
  • Entry. Every other failure in processing a transaction_data entry for a credential, in this or any other PaSO specification, makes the entry not compatible with that credential. What follows is decided by Section 7.3 step 2 in the simple profile and by Section 7.4.2 steps 2 to 4 in the advanced profile.

The following summary is informative. For each entry and candidate credential, the Wallet determines the definition of the type as follows:

  1. If the entry carries a metadata parameter, the Wallet verifies it per [PaSO Proof Metadata] Section 5.3. Invalid ad-hoc metadata makes the entry incompatible, without fallback to the stored credential metadata. Valid ad-hoc metadata is the definition of the type for this transaction: the payload is checked against it and, where the Wallet implements a rulebook for the type, also against that rulebook (condition 3). The entry is rendered dynamically ([PaSO View] Section 5.1).
  2. Otherwise, the type is supported only if the signed credential metadata lists it (condition 2). The payload is checked against that metadata and, where the Wallet implements it, against the rulebook (condition 3).
  3. The Wallet then selects the rendering mode: static rendering where [PaSO View] Section 5.1 permits it, and dynamic rendering from the metadata otherwise.

docs.title: A.2 KB-JWT Payload (SD-JWT-VC)

docs.title: A.5 Advanced Profile — Multiple Transaction Data Entries
docs.text:
A Relying Party accepts either a card or an account PaSO Credential, and optionally a PID. Each transaction_data entry targets a different credential via credential_ids:

{
  "dcql_query": {
    "credentials": [
      {
        "id": "sca_card",
        "format": "dc+sd-jwt",
        "meta": { "vct_values": ["https://bank.example/sca/card"] }
      },
      {
        "id": "sca_account",
        "format": "dc+sd-jwt",
        "meta": { "vct_values": ["https://bank.example/sca/account"] }
      },
      {
        "id": "pid",
        "format": "dc+sd-jwt",
        "meta": { "vct_values": ["https://credentials.example/pid"] },
        "claims": [
          { "path": ["given_name"] },
          { "path": ["family_name"] }
        ]
      }
    ],
    "credential_sets": [
      {
        "options": [
          ["sca_card", "pid"],
          ["sca_card"],
          ["sca_account", "pid"],
          ["sca_account"]
        ]
      }
    ]
  }
}

Decoded transaction_data entries:

[
  {
    "type": "urn:paso:sca:global:payment:1",
    "credential_ids": ["sca_card"],
    "payload": {
      "transaction_id": "ab9c4d5e-6f78-9012-3456-789abcdef012",
      "amount": "49.99 EUR",
      "payee": { "name": "Shop Inc.", "id": "DE98ZZZ09999999999" }
    }
  },
  {
    "type": "urn:paso:sca:global:payment:1",
    "credential_ids": ["sca_account"],
    "payload": {
      "transaction_id": "ab9c4d5e-6f78-9012-3456-789abcdef012",
      "amount": "49.99 EUR",
      "payee": { "name": "Shop Inc.", "id": "DE98ZZZ09999999999" }
    }
  }
]

The four alternatives decompose into S₁ = {sca_card, sca_account}, S₂ = {pid, ∅}. S₁ is the PaSO slot (Section 7.4.1). The user independently chooses which PaSO Credential to use and whether to include the PID. When the user switches from sca_card to sca_account, the displayed transaction data updates to reflect the entry matched for that credential.

docs.title: A.6 Advanced Profile — Transposability
docs.text:
Example (transposable): A Relying Party accepts one PaSO Credential (sca_card) and optionally requests a PID from two possible issuers (pid_1 and pid_2):

"options": [
  ["sca_card", "pid_1"],
  ["sca_card", "pid_2"],
  ["sca_card"]
]

This decomposes into S₁ = {sca_card}, S₂ = {pid_1, pid_2, ∅}. The user is presented two independent choices: sca_card (mandatory), and optionally which PID to include.

Counterexample (not transposable): The Relying Party also optionally accepts a loyalty credential, but only in combination with pid_2:

"options": [
  ["sca_card", "pid_1"],
  ["sca_card", "pid_2", "loyalty"],
  ["sca_card"]
]

The only candidate decomposition would be S₁ = {sca_card}, S₂ = {pid_1, pid_2, ∅}, S₃ = {loyalty, ∅}, which requires six alternatives, not three. The Relying Party has created an artificial dependency between loyalty and pid_2. A Wallet SHALL reject this request.

To make it transposable, the Relying Party must include all six combinations:

"options": [
  ["sca_card", "pid_1", "loyalty"],
  ["sca_card", "pid_1"],
  ["sca_card", "pid_2", "loyalty"],
  ["sca_card", "pid_2"],
  ["sca_card", "loyalty"],
  ["sca_card"]
]

docs.title: A.7 Advanced Profile — Versioned Transaction Data
docs.text:
A Relying Party has migrated its transaction type from version 1 to version 2, which adds an optional reward_points claim. The Relying Party lists the newer type first so that credentials supporting it use the richer payload, while older credentials fall back to v1:

Decoded transaction_data entries:

[
  {
    "type": "urn:paso:sca:com.example.pay:transaction:2",
    "credential_ids": ["sca"],
    "payload": {
      "transaction_id": "ab9c4d5e-6f78-9012-3456-789abcdef012",
      "amount": "49.99 EUR",
      "payee": { "name": "Example Shop", "id": "DE98ZZZ09999999999" },
      "reward_points": "150"
    }
  },
  {
    "type": "urn:paso:sca:com.example.pay:transaction:1",
    "credential_ids": ["sca"],
    "payload": {
      "transaction_id": "ab9c4d5e-6f78-9012-3456-789abcdef012",
      "amount": "49.99 EUR",
      "payee": { "name": "Example Shop", "id": "DE98ZZZ09999999999" }
    }
  }
]

Both entries target the same credential_ids. When the Wallet evaluates the user's credential:

  • If the credential supports urn:paso:sca:com.example.pay:transaction:2, the first entry matches and is selected.
  • If the credential only supports urn:paso:sca:com.example.pay:transaction:1, the first entry is skipped and the second entry is selected.

This allows the Relying Party to roll out a new transaction data version without breaking compatibility with credentials that have not yet been updated.

docs.title: Abstract
docs.text: This document defines how Wallets render transaction data for user consent. It specifies the generic rendering procedure, the normative set of value types for formatting claim values and labels, the locale selection procedure, and the UI elements used during a transaction.

docs.title: 1.1 Overview
docs.text:
[PaSO Proof Metadata] defines how credential metadata carries transaction data type definitions, including claims with display arrays and value_type hints. This document defines how the Wallet uses that metadata to render transaction data to the user.

This document defines two rendering modes. In dynamic rendering, the Wallet renders any transaction data type generically using the metadata alone — no transaction-type-specific logic is required. The Wallet SHALL be able to render every transaction data type with dynamic rendering. For transaction data types whose Transaction Data Type Rulebook contains a Static Presentation section, the Wallet MAY instead use static rendering, a purpose-built consent screen with Wallet-defined layout and labels, as defined in Section 5.

PaSO View applies to both the simple and the advanced profile defined in [PaSO Core] Section 7. Whenever the user's credential selection changes which credential or transaction_data entry applies, the Wallet renders the transaction data anew per this document.

docs.title: 1.2 Requirements Notation
docs.text: The key words "MUST", "MUST NOT", "REQUIRED", "SHALL", "SHALL NOT", "SHOULD", "SHOULD NOT", "RECOMMENDED", "MAY", and "OPTIONAL" in this document are to be interpreted as described in [RFC2119] and [RFC8174] when, and only when, they are written in all capital letters.

docs.title: 2 Generic Rendering
docs.text:
This section defines dynamic rendering. Section 5.3 specifies which of its requirements also apply to static rendering.

The Wallet SHALL be able to render any transaction data type generically. All claims that have a display array SHALL be rendered as a sequence of labelled values. Claims without a display array MUST be internal values irrelevant to the user's consent; the Wallet MAY omit them from the consent screen or show them in a separate detailed view.

The display order SHALL be the order in which the claims appear in the claims array, not the order of fields in the payload object.

Each label SHALL be rendered as plain text. Each value SHALL be formatted according to its value_type as defined in Section 3.

The Wallet SHALL ensure that all claims with a display array, and all populated UI elements — including the security_hint where present — have been displayed to the user before enabling the confirmation action.

Relying Parties and Attestation Providers MUST NOT use labels, payload values, or hints to obfuscate information relevant to the user's consent.

The Wallet SHALL populate the UI elements defined in [PaSO Proof Metadata] Section 3.2 with the localised labels from the credential metadata. When a security_hint is present, the Wallet SHALL display it exactly as provided.

All labels are subject to the length limits and character constraints defined in [PaSO Proof Metadata] Section 3.3. The Wallet SHALL verify these constraints for every label it renders. If any label violates a constraint, the transaction_data entry is not compatible and the Wallet SHALL exclude it. The Wallet MUST NOT truncate, elide, or otherwise shorten a label; it MAY wrap a label across multiple lines provided the text remains visible in full. The Wallet SHALL likewise exclude a transaction_data entry whose formatted claim values contain the directional formatting characters prohibited by [PaSO Proof Metadata] Section 3.3.

The Wallet SHALL be capable of displaying any label that conforms to the maximum lengths of [PaSO Proof Metadata] Section 3.3 in full, in every display configuration the Wallet supports — including platform accessibility text scaling. For action labels this MAY include wrapping the label across multiple lines, enlarging the control, or reducing the font size within the limits of legibility; the Wallet MUST NOT rely on platform default controls that truncate or ellipsize overflowing text. If, despite this, a conforming label cannot be displayed in full in the active display configuration, the Wallet SHALL NOT proceed with a partially displayed label: the transaction_data entry SHALL be treated as not compatible, and if no compatible entry remains, the Wallet SHALL cease processing and inform the user of the reason.

When claims contain null (array wildcard) in their path, the Wallet SHALL render them using the following recursive rule. For a given set of claims at a given nesting level:

  1. Render all claims whose remaining path contains no null, in declared order.
  2. Group the remaining claims by their shared path prefix up to and including the first null. For each such group, in the order of its first declared claim, iterate over the array elements at the null position: for each element, apply this rule recursively to the group's claims with the null resolved to that element's index.

The Wallet SHOULD display the complete transaction data on a single screen. Where this is not feasible, the Wallet MAY use scrolling, collapsible sections, or detailed views, provided the user can review the content in its entirety and the Wallet ensures the content has been displayed in full before enabling the confirmation action.

A transaction_data entry MUST NOT contain more than 10 displayed claim values. Displayed claim values are the instances, present in the payload, of claims that have a display array, counted after array wildcard expansion. UI elements do not count toward this limit. The count is the same in dynamic and static rendering, even where static rendering omits a claim. The Wallet SHALL be able to render 10 displayed claim values. A transaction_data entry that exceeds this limit is not compatible and the Wallet SHALL exclude it.

docs.title: 3 Value Types
docs.text:
Each claim metadata object that has a display array MAY include a value_type parameter that indicates how the Wallet SHALL format the claim value for display. If value_type is omitted, the value is treated as plain text and MUST be a string. The value_type parameter MUST NOT be used on claims without a display array.

The Wallet SHALL support all value types defined below. A transaction_data entry whose displayable claims declare a value_type not supported by the Wallet, or whose payload values do not conform to the declared value_type, is not compatible and the Wallet SHALL exclude it.

Labels — the name of a claim's display entry and the value of a ui_labels entry — are plain text. Value types apply to claim values only and MUST NOT be applied to labels.

value_typeDescription boolean The value is a JSON boolean (true or false). The Wallet SHALL display it as a localised human-readable string or a clear and unmistakable graphical representation. frequency The value is one of the following frequency codes: `INDA` (intraday), `DAIL` (daily), `WEEK` (weekly), `TOWK` (every two weeks), `TWMN` (twice a month), `MNTH` (monthly), `TOMN` (every two months), `QUTR` (quarterly), `FOMN` (every four months), `SEMI` (twice a year), `YEAR` (yearly), `TYEA` (every two years). The Wallet **SHALL** display it as a human-readable, localised string that accurately and unmistakably represents the frequency. image The value is a string containing a resolvable URL or a Data URL per [RFC2397] pointing to an image. Images serve an informational or illustrative purpose; the user is not required to view them to give informed consent. The image **MUST** be in PNG or JPEG format; an image in any other format makes the `transaction_data` entry not compatible. When resolving a URL, the Wallet **SHALL** send an `Accept` header listing `image/png` and `image/jpeg`. If the URL is not a Data URL, it **MUST** use the `https` scheme and the `payload` **MUST** contain a sibling claim at the same path suffixed with `#integrity` containing a [W3C.SRI] hash of the image content. The Wallet **SHALL** resolve the URL and verify the content against the `#integrity` value. When resolving, the Wallet **SHALL** enforce a fetch timeout, **SHALL** follow at most 3 redirects, and **SHALL NOT** transmit cookies, credentials, or Wallet-identifying headers. If verification fails, the `transaction_data` entry is not compatible. An image — the Data URL payload or the resolved content — **MUST NOT** exceed 512 KiB in encoded size, and its decoded dimensions **MUST NOT** exceed 2048 pixels in either direction. A non-conforming image makes the `transaction_data` entry not compatible. Because images are informational only, they **MUST NOT** convey information required for the user's consent. The Wallet **SHALL** render images contained within the consent layout; an image **SHALL NOT** overlay or displace other transaction data or Wallet controls. See Section 6.3 for the linkability considerations of resolving remote images. iso_date The value is an [ISO8601] date string. The Wallet SHALL display it in a user-friendly localised date format that accurately and unmistakably represents the date. iso_time The value is an [ISO8601] time string. The Wallet SHALL display it in a user-friendly localised time format that accurately and unmistakably represents the time. iso_date_time The value is an [ISO8601] date-time string. The Wallet SHALL display it in a user-friendly localised date-time format that accurately and unmistakably represents the date and time. iso_currency The value is an [ISO4217] Alpha-3 currency code string. The Wallet MAY display it in a user-friendly format (e.g., the currency symbol or full name) that accurately and unmistakably identifies the currency. iso_currency_amount The value is a string consisting of a decimal number (integer part, decimal point, fractional digits per [ISO4217]) followed by a space and an [ISO4217] Alpha-3 currency code (e.g., `"49.99 EUR"`). The Wallet **MAY** display it in a user-friendly localised format that accurately and unmistakably represents the amount and currency. label_only The Wallet **SHALL** render only the `name` from the locale-matched `display` entry, without any associated value. This type is intended for contexts where no value is needed to convey the meaning, such as informational statements (e.g., "This is a recurring payment"). The claim **MUST NOT** be `mandatory`. The value in the `payload` **MAY** be of any JSON type. url The value is a string containing a navigatable URL. URLs serve an informational or illustrative purpose; the user is not required to view them to give informed consent. The URL **MUST** use the `https` scheme; otherwise the `transaction_data` entry is not compatible. The Wallet **SHALL** display it as a clearly identifiable link. The Wallet **SHALL** display the full URL to the user; it **MUST NOT** replace or obscure the URL with alternative text. The Wallet **SHOULD** mitigate homograph confusion, e.g. by displaying an internationalised domain name in its punycode form when it contains confusable characters. The Wallet **SHOULD NOT** make the URL navigable directly from the consent screen. If navigation is offered, it **SHALL** require an explicit user action clearly distinct from the consent actions, and the Wallet **SHOULD** indicate that the user is leaving the Wallet.

docs.title: 4 Locale Selection
docs.text:
This section applies to dynamic rendering, and to static rendering where a security_hint is present (Section 5.4).

The Wallet SHALL maintain a locale priority list: an ordered sequence of [RFC5646] language tags representing the user's language preferences, in decreasing order of priority.

The Wallet SHALL render all display entries and ui_labels entries of a transaction either from a single locale or entirely from default entries (entries without a locale). It SHALL NOT combine entries of different locales, or locale-tagged and default entries, on one consent screen.

The arrays considered are the display arrays of all claims metadata objects that have one, together with all ui_labels entry arrays, for the matching transaction data type. The available tags are the locale values for which every considered array has an entry, compared case-insensitively.

The Wallet SHALL select the locale as follows:

  1. For each locale in the priority list, in order, apply the Lookup matching scheme defined in [RFC4647] Section 3.4, using that locale as the language range and the available tags as the set of language tags to match against. On the first match, the matched tag is selected. The Wallet SHALL render every considered array from its entry with that tag and SHALL NOT continue.
  2. If no locale in the priority list produced a match, and every considered array has a default entry, the default entries are selected. The Wallet SHALL render every considered array from its default entry.
  3. Otherwise, the transaction_data entry is not compatible with the credential ([PaSO Core] Section 7.5).

A locale-tagged match for any locale in the priority list takes precedence over the default entries. The Wallet SHALL NOT treat a transaction_data entry as not compatible solely because the default entries were selected.

The Wallet SHALL report the selection in the display_locale holder binding proof claim per [PaSO Core]. The reported value is the selected tag as it appears in the metadata locale values, or the string default if the default entries were selected. It is not the priority-list locale used as the language range.

If the transaction data cannot be presented in the Wallet's current operating language, the Wallet MAY switch its entire user interface to another language the user understands for the duration of the PaSO presentation flow.

docs.title: 5.1 Eligibility
docs.text:
The Wallet MAY render a transaction_data entry with static rendering only if all of the following hold:

  1. The applicable Transaction Data Type Rulebook contains a Static Presentation section per [PaSO Core] Section 5.3.
  2. The Wallet implements that rulebook for the exact transaction data type identifier of the entry, including its version.
  3. The entry does not carry an ad-hoc metadata parameter per [PaSO Proof Metadata] Section 5.

Otherwise, the Wallet SHALL use dynamic rendering.

docs.title: 5.2 Mode Selection
docs.text:
The Wallet selects the rendering mode for each transaction_data entry it presents. Attestation Providers and Relying Parties cannot require or prohibit static rendering. The mode applies to the entry presented with the selected PaSO Credential and MAY differ between the candidate credentials the user can choose from ([PaSO Core] Sections 7.3 and 7.4). The Wallet SHALL report the mode used for the presented entry in the render_mode claim per [PaSO Core] Section 6.1.

Static rendering does not change how the credential metadata is obtained or which transaction data types a credential supports. The Wallet SHALL retrieve and verify the signed credential metadata per [PaSO Proof Metadata], and the payload SHALL conform both to the Transaction Data Type Rulebook and to the claims metadata of the matched transaction data type.

docs.title: 5.3 Presentation Obligations
docs.text:
In static rendering, the Wallet SHALL display the content that the Static Presentation section of the rulebook requires, in the manner it requires. The Wallet uses its own layout and its own localised labels in place of the display entries and ui_labels of the credential metadata, except for the security_hint. The Wallet's labels SHALL convey the meaning defined by the rulebook clearly and unmistakably.

The following requirements of Section 2 apply to static rendering unchanged: all content required for display SHALL have been displayed before the confirmation action is enabled; the Wallet MUST NOT truncate, elide, or otherwise shorten any label or displayed claim value; displayed claim values SHALL be formatted according to their value_type per Section 3; a transaction_data entry whose formatted claim values contain prohibited directional formatting characters SHALL be excluded; and the limit on displayed claim values applies.

When the matched transaction data type provides a security_hint, the Wallet SHALL display it exactly as provided, in the entry selected per Section 5.4.

docs.title: 5.4 Locale and display_locale
docs.text:
A statically rendered consent screen SHALL use a single language.

If the matched transaction data type provides a security_hint, the Wallet SHALL perform locale selection per Section 4. If that selects the default entries, or selects a tag in whose language the Wallet cannot render its static presentation, the Wallet SHALL use dynamic rendering instead. Otherwise, the Wallet SHALL render the static presentation in the language of the selected tag and SHALL report the selected tag in display_locale.

If no security_hint is provided, the Wallet SHALL report in display_locale the [RFC5646] language tag of the language in which it rendered the static presentation.

In static rendering, display_locale SHALL NOT be default.

docs.title: 6 Security Considerations
docs.text: Note: This section is informative.

docs.title: 6.1 Metadata as an Injection Channel
docs.text: Everything the Wallet renders during consent originates outside the Wallet: labels and value types from the Attestation Provider's signed metadata, and — through value formatting — values from the Relying Party's payload. The constraints in this document and in [PaSO Proof Metadata] Section 3.3 (length limits, character prohibitions, text-only labels, resource limits, rendering caps) exist to keep this channel from being usable to obfuscate or forge consent content. Wallets should treat every metadata- or payload-supplied string strictly as display data — never as markup beyond the constructs explicitly permitted by the declared value type, and never as code or instructions.

docs.title: 6.2 Why Truncation Is Prohibited
docs.text: Section 2 forbids truncating, eliding, or shortening labels. Attacker-influenced text truncates to attacker-chosen prefixes: a label crafted so that platform ellipsis cuts it after "Confirm payment of €1.00" hides the continuation. Divergent, implementation-defined truncation behaviour across Wallets would make such attacks reliable. Exclusion of the entire entry is therefore the only permitted failure mode for oversized content.

docs.title: 6.3 Linkability of Remote Resources
docs.text: Resolving a remote image URL at consent time reveals the transaction timing and the Wallet's network address to the host serving the image. Attestation Providers and Relying Parties should prefer Data URLs for images. Wallets resolving remote images should be aware of this correlation channel; the considerations of [PaSO Proof Metadata] Section 8 on unlinkability apply in spirit, even though the fetch is triggered by the transaction itself.

docs.title: 6.4 Confusable Text and Wallet Chrome Spoofing
docs.text: The character constraints prohibit directional embedding and override characters, but cannot prevent homoglyphs or text that mimics Wallet UI (e.g., a label reading "✓ Verified by your Wallet"). Wallets should render metadata-supplied content so that it is visually attributable as transaction content and cannot be mistaken for Wallet-generated UI or system dialogs — for example, through clear containment within the consent layout and consistent, Wallet-controlled styling of its own controls.

docs.title: 6.5 Why the Number of Displayed Claim Values Is Limited
docs.text: A user can realistically review only a small number of values before confirming a transaction; a consent screen that lists more invites approval without review. Section 2 therefore fixes the limit at 10 displayed claim values for every Wallet rather than leaving it Wallet-defined: a single limit makes behaviour identical across Wallets, so a transaction cannot be presentable in one Wallet and rejected by another, and every Wallet can design its consent screen for a known maximum. A transaction_data entry over the limit is excluded rather than shortened, for the reasons given in Section 6.2.

docs.title: A.1 Locale Selection
docs.text:
The following examples apply Section 4 to the transaction data type of [PaSO Proof Metadata] Annex A.6. Every array in that metadata carries entries for en and de and a default entry, so the available tags are en and de, and the default entries are available as a fallback.

Wallet locale priority list Lookup Entries rendered display_locale de, en de matches de de de de-CH de-CH truncates to de, which matches de de fr, de fr no match; de matches de de fr no match default default

In the third row, German is shown although the first preference, fr, is unavailable: a locale-tagged match anywhere in the priority list takes precedence over the default entries. In the fourth row, the user sees the issuer's fallback text, and the proof says so: display_locale is default, not fr.

If the same metadata carried no default entries, the fourth row would produce no selection, and the transaction_data entry would not be compatible with the credential.

docs.title: Abstract
docs.text: This document defines the audit logging requirements for PaSO. It specifies what the Wallet must retain for each PaSO Credential and each PaSO transaction to enable a full user-side audit trail.

docs.title: 1 Introduction
docs.text: This module defines a user-side audit log for PaSO. It does not mandate a particular storage format or schema. It specifies what data the Wallet must retain so that any transaction can be independently reconstructed and verified.

docs.title: 1.1 Requirements Notation
docs.text: The key words "MUST", "MUST NOT", "REQUIRED", "SHALL", "SHALL NOT", "SHOULD", "SHOULD NOT", "RECOMMENDED", "MAY", and "OPTIONAL" in this document are to be interpreted as described in [RFC2119] and [RFC8174] when, and only when, they are written in all capital letters.

docs.title: 2 Credential Storage
docs.text:
For each PaSO Credential, the Wallet SHALL store the following artefacts together:

  1. The credential itself, in the format as received from the Attestation Provider.

  2. Metadata history: all signed credential metadata JWTs (per [PaSO Proof Metadata]) used during presentations, including all locale variants.

  3. Resolved resources: all external resources fetched for credential display. For each resource, the Wallet SHALL store:

  4. the URL from which the resource was retrieved,
  5. the resource content,
  6. its [W3C.SRI] integrity value,
  7. the date and time of retrieval.

docs.title: 3 Transaction Storage
docs.text:
For each [OID4VP] presentation session involving PaSO transaction data, whether completed or not, the Wallet SHALL store:

  1. The [OID4VP] Authorization Request as received by the Wallet.

  2. The full vp_token as delivered to the Relying Party. If the transaction was not completed, whatever was produced at the point of abandonment, or nothing if no token was generated.

  3. Resolved resources: all external resources fetched during the transaction for transaction display, such as remote images. For each resource, the Wallet SHALL store:

  4. the URL from which the resource was retrieved,
  5. the resource content,
  6. its [W3C.SRI] integrity value,

  7. the date and time of retrieval.

  8. The date and time of the transaction.

docs.title: 4 Export
docs.text: The Wallet MAY support exporting the transaction log and credential artefacts.

docs.title: 5 Replayability
docs.text: The Wallet SHOULD provide a mechanism to replay the full presentation request exactly as it happened at that time, with the credential choices set to the ones that were chosen at that time. Where the presentation was rendered with static rendering (render_mode static, per [PaSO View] Section 5), the replay SHALL reproduce the static presentation of the Wallet version identified by wallet_instance_version.
